This PR was part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #44994 (merged)
* #44993 (merged)
* #44991 (merged)
* #44480 (merged)

## Motivation

Model forwards can omit expert placement or the live token count, routing logical IDs against physical expert weights or processing padding as real tokens. Move those decisions into TopK and the active forward. Automatic padding also makes inactive routes reachable at EP1, so every affected consumer must skip their data, weights and expert addresses safely.

## Modifications

- Resolve placement per call and capture draft identity during construction. Align draft weight loading with identity routing, including in-range draft layer IDs; retain target placement-aware loading.
- Bind the prepared ForwardBatch across eager execution, graph capture/replay, CPU graphs and TBO children. Bind copied row/tail batches too. Decline DeepSeek row-tail capture when its MoE count is a separate GLOBAL buffer, using the existing eager path.
- Preserve lazy routing metadata until materialization. Keep the producing layer ID in TopKConfig, including piecewise reconstruction, so lazy LP conversion defaults to the correct solver while explicit overrides (including 0) still win. Keep the existing five-field tuple ABI. Reject logits-only consumers that cannot apply required remapping. Route DeepSeek graph admission through the same layer contract. Keep shared expert columns outside LP solving and routed-only remapping.
- Make Triton, Marlin, GGUF, W4AFP8 and Humming consumers honor inactive routes independently of EP, including NaN inputs/weights and poisoned intermediate buffers. Generic Marlin reuses its projection allocation, clearing the down view after activation consumes the up view; LoRA retains separate zeroed buffers.
- Support the published `sglang-kernel==0.4.10` GGUF provider with Python block-size selection, safe vector indices, masked inactive intermediates/contributions, and initialized MMQ slack metadata. Retain the AOT source fixes for future wheel builds.
- Initialize CUTLASS FP8 gather maps and use a masked Triton reduction that skips inactive data and weights. Pass token count and supported weight strides at runtime without value specialization so new lengths reuse compiled kernels. This fixes both block-FP8 and MXFP8 without requiring a newly released AOT wheel.
- Reject LongCat zero-expert placement configurations at startup, since routed-only placement tables cannot represent its identity experts safely. Plain identity placement remains available.
- Assert the Marlin allocation property rather than an incidental `.zero_()` call; set its CI runtime estimate to 720 seconds to cover cold compilation.

## CI repairs and validation

Current head: `2447ebc8cd21ba19ceb5f94c67826d30ff4aeaa0`; base #44993 is `4275a5026050615139c3658a72b6a7d05d65b17f`. Updated by normal fast-forward pushes.

Two latest repairs:

- Shared-expert routing fixture: publishing TP=1 and then overriding EP=8 failed topology validation before routing. Supply a consistent virtual TP=EP=8 topology at rank 3, without process groups or collectives. Registration and numerical assertions are unchanged. On one NVIDIA H200, the original complete file produced seven topology subtest errors; the repaired file passed all four tests at both stack production revisions, including five CUDA router variants, shared contribution and fullgraph compile behavior.
- AMD AITER prefill: eager draft extend selected a new query-offset table in `ForwardMetadata`, while CK still received the backend's stale prompt table. Measured Q had 80 rows but the passed offsets reached 4,648, immediately followed by the GPU memory fault. Publish ordinary prefill offsets into the same metadata owner and consume that owner's view in CK, ASM and 5D prefill. Kernel selection, KV padding and speculative helpers are unchanged. [#40872](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40872) describes the same defect with a producer-side repair; this patch keeps the existing per-forward owner authoritative at consumers.

AMD before/after: the unchanged EAGLE canary failed with a memory fault on both this stack and its original main base. After repair, all 20 requests and original assertions passed (50.6s process). A second serialized observation run passed too: CK received `[0,4,...,80]`, all 588 eager CK calls returned, and no malformed query CSR or HSA fault was observed. Decode graphs and all test assertions remained enabled as configured. Hardware: one AMD MI350X; original CI used MI300. Torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0, AITER 2bb549102, CK 96afae1d5. NHD/BF16 is exercised; the corresponding 5D/FP8/ASM corrections have source review coverage. Final source differs from the tested repair only by removing a stale comment. Independent source review and configured pre-commit checks passed.

H200 fixture runtime: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, FlashInfer 0.6.18. This is single-GPU routing validation, not eight-GPU collective or full-model validation.

Other failures in the latest CI run:

- JIT B200 failed before tests: its local wheel was truncated to 94 MiB and lacked a ZIP central directory. A sibling verified the same artifact and installed its full 356 MiB wheel successfully (4,821 tests passed). A clean artifact download/retry is needed; no retry was triggered here.
- Qwen3-Next FP8 HiCache multi-turn KL exceeded its unchanged threshold. The same production code passed this method in the preceding run. The local numerical A/B ran zero comparisons: its Rust cache extension could not build against Torch 2.14.1. No version-check bypass was applied. This failure remains unattributed; no numerical fix or passing baseline is claimed.
- AMD disaggregation failed at startup with HIP OOM, also seen in an earlier main run. The AITER query-offset fix addresses the separately reproduced EAGLE memory fault, and does not claim to fix this startup failure.
- NPU QwenImage has identical failing metrics in three unrelated PR runs with the same expected image. A scoped source audit found no changed numerical path from this MoE stack, but no bare-base NPU A/B was run and its root cause remains unresolved.

Earlier CI-only repairs at `0a3e1cfa68` remain included: inherited DeepSeek dual-stream fixture correction from #44993, current activation import, Bailing NextN/V3 parity ownership, and Python 3.11 wheel selection in the simulator job. Their recorded validation was 54 quantization tests, 85 kernel namespace tests, the complete DeepSeek opcheck/compile/graph-replay test at both production revisions, two parity tests, 49 fusion-gate tests plus 11 subtests, and artifact-name matching. Those checks were not rerun for these bounded changes. Full CI and full-model acceptance remain pending; earlier validation below stays tied to its named revisions.

## Earlier validation after rebase

Head: `5a0a941ff3013d5c98cff1a5854d03bebff7324c`. Rebased onto main `553836c1647b3bfbeb266b49d76ec2c9df012425`; base `cheng/refactor/moe-layer-backend-semantics` is `fc2dd3d90bf86fe1b61741c1bb8d28a4e121dc8a`.

- At this exact head, 6 focused CPU module(s) passed: 66 tests plus 115 reported subtests. Across all four PR heads, 15 focused modules completed 482 test executions plus 347 reported subtests, all passing.
- Each PR's full incremental tree matches the pre-rebase change applied to its rewritten base, retaining prior merge-only integration fixes. The stack remains #44480 -> #44991 -> #44993 -> #44994.
- Configured pre-commit checks passed over all 152 changed files in the full stack. Strict registration/entrypoint checks passed: 2,478 files / 3,012 registrations. CPU tests used Python 3.12.15 and Torch 2.14.1+cu130 with GPUs hidden.

GPU, full-model accuracy/throughput and full CI were not rerun for this rebase. Prior hardware measurements below remain evidence for their named earlier revisions; checked CUTLASS/Marlin/GGUF consumer sources are unchanged, which is source evidence rather than a new GPU run.

## Previous validation (before rebase)

Previous head: `068e12b7c155babfdc6eea074812b12c7830a3df`, including #44993 at `b37b73a1ae1bdf3d73b6108deb76a14679a079b4`, all lower PRs, and main `693d33330647c57f82e09ac39a34122fa46b5763`.

- At this exact integrated head, 12 focused CPU modules passed: 119 tests plus 200 reported subtests. Coverage includes lazy LP ownership, routing metadata/graph bounds, dispatcher contracts, shared/routed scale, native model policy admission, ModelOpt/FP8 ownership, runner extensions and placement. The lower PR was also checked independently. New regressions fail against their pre-fix production sources for the intended conditions.
- All 3 CUTLASS FP8 CUDA test methods passed on one NVIDIA B300, including real native block-FP8/MXFP8 GEMMs and mixed/all-inactive graph replay. The reduction test spans 12 token counts, contiguous/transposed weights, FP16/BF16 and poisoned NaN routes. The old real Triton cache grew to 23 entries per dtype; the fixed kernel retains 1. Tested kernel/test bytes are unchanged by the final merge.
- Native environment: Python 3.12.15, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2 and published `sglang-kernel 0.4.10`. Incompatible FlashInfer 0.7.1 cubin/cache packages were ignored; kernels compiled as needed.
- Configured hooks passed on all 11 files touched in this round. Strict registration/entrypoint checks pass: 2,472 files / 3,006 registrations.

Earlier validation at the preceding heads remains historical: 856 CPU tests across 43 modules with 7 skips, 18 native Marlin cases, 2 prior CUTLASS FP8 methods and 4 GGUF cases against the published 0.4.10 wheel. The new focused CPU and 3-method CUTLASS runs above replace the corresponding coverage for this revision; the Marlin/GGUF kernels are unchanged this round.

The earlier reduced Qwen3 TP4/EP4 reverse-placement graph smoke matched 72 generated IDs and logprobs at its recorded revision; it was not rerun as full-model validation here. No new all-valid reduction latency, dropped-block scan cost or serving throughput measurement is claimed. Native TRT-LLM selector parity, full-model accuracy, ROCm/NPU/AMX and external FlashInfer/HPC/KT consumer coverage remain unverified. Full CI has not been established for this head.

## Main integration for merge

Current head: `ad06555c737b78c7767cba9b51e0c2ba6305b8ed`. Integrated main at `533020b500ba781bfafd1f5cbadabaf03d8986f7` with a history-preserving merge.

Retained TopK's ownership of per-call routing inputs, combined draft identity placement with main's explicit `uses_expert_location` API, preserved main's gfx1250 expert-parallel support, and reconciled the dispatcher and MegaMoE fixtures. Removed an automatically restored Qwen3 model-side dispatch input; the model routing audit found no remaining legacy inputs across 297 model files.

Independent static review and the normal configured pre-commit hooks passed for these integration changes. Unit/GPU tests and CI were not rerun for this landing; earlier results remain tied to their stated revisions. The two reviewed Muse/W4A8 allocation costs will be repaired in a separate follow-up PR.
